_metadata.description: Cited ingredient knowledge base. Each entry carries claims with named sources. Distinct from server/data/substances (regulatory evidence + policy), which decides risk levels; this file supplies the readable cited claims shown to users.
_metadata.reviewPolicy: Entries seeded by AI start as reviewStatus=ai_seeded and MUST be verified by a qualified human reviewer (statement wording + source attribution) before marketing claims cite them. Set reviewStatus=human_reviewed and fill reviewedBy/reviewedAt after verification.

claims.statement: Oral retinoids are established teratogens; major medical bodies advise avoiding topical retinoids during pregnancy as a precaution, even though absorbed doses are low.

sources.title: Skin Conditions During Pregnancy (patient guidance on retinoid avoidance)
Isotretinoin iPLEDGE REMS (teratogenicity of retinoids)

claims.statement: No longer generally recognized as safe and effective for OTC sale in the US (CARES Act, 2020); banned in cosmetics in the EU. Systemic absorption is comparatively high, so use in pregnancy is commonly advised against.

sources.title: Hydroquinone in over-the-counter drug products — regulatory status after the CARES Act
Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex II (prohibited substances)

claims.statement: Formaldehyde is classified as carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1); the listed preservatives release small amounts of formaldehyde over time and are common contact-allergy triggers.

sources.title: IARC Monographs Vol. 100F — Formaldehyde
Formaldehyde-releasing preservatives as contact allergens

claims.statement: A leading cause of preservative contact allergy; the EU banned methylisothiazolinone in leave-on cosmetics (2017) and restricts it in rinse-off products.

sources.title: Opinions on methylisothiazolinone; Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1224
Methylisothiazolinone — Allergen of the Year

claims.statement: FDA revoked authorization for Red No. 3 in foods and ingested drugs (January 2025) based on carcinogenicity in male rats; long banned in US cosmetics.

sources.title: FDA to Revoke Authorization for the Use of Red No. 3 in Food and Ingested Drugs

claims.statement: EU requires the warning 'may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children' on foods containing these dyes, following the Southampton study; the US requires no such label.

sources.title: Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 on food additives, Annex V
Scientific opinions re-evaluating Southampton-study food colours

claims.statement: EFSA concluded titanium dioxide can no longer be considered safe as a food additive (genotoxicity could not be ruled out); the EU banned E171 in food from 2022. It remains permitted in US food and in cosmetics.

sources.title: Safety assessment of titanium dioxide (E171) as a food additive
Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/63 banning E171 in food

claims.statement: Classified as possibly carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 2B) and listed under California Proposition 65; permitted in the US and EU within limits.

sources.title: IARC Monographs Vol. 40 — Butylated hydroxyanisole
Proposition 65 chemical list — BHA

claims.statement: Evidence is mixed: not classified as a human carcinogen; EFSA maintains an acceptable daily intake. Some consumers avoid it alongside BHA; EU permits within limits.

sources.title: Scientific Opinion on the re-evaluation of butylated hydroxytoluene (E321)

claims.statement: The EU banned five parabens in cosmetics (2014) and restricts propyl-/butylparaben concentrations over endocrine-activity concerns; shorter-chain parabens (methyl-, ethyl-) are considered safe at permitted levels.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 358/2014 and (EU) No 1004/2014 (parabens)
Opinion on parabens (SCCS/1514/13)

claims.statement: Banned in cosmetics in the EU; classified as reproductive toxicants. Sometimes present undeclared in 'fragrance'. Particular caution advised in pregnancy.

sources.title: Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex II — phthalates
Phthalates factsheet (National Biomonitoring Program)

claims.statement: IARC classified aspartame as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B, 2023) while JECFA reaffirmed the existing acceptable daily intake; people with phenylketonuria must avoid it (phenylalanine source).

sources.title: Aspartame hazard and risk assessment results
Aspartame and Other Sweeteners in Food

claims.statement: IARC classifies talc as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A, 2024 re-evaluation); historical concerns center on asbestos contamination and perineal use. FDA runs an annual asbestos-testing program for talc cosmetics.

sources.title: IARC Monographs Vol. 136 — Talc
Talc in cosmetics — testing for asbestos

claims.statement: FDA's proposed sunscreen rule (2019) found insufficient data to classify oxybenzone as generally recognized as safe and effective, citing systemic absorption; banned for reef protection in Hawaii.

sources.title: Proposed rule: Sunscreen Drug Products for OTC Human Use
Act 104 (SB 2571) — oxybenzone/octinoxate sunscreen ban

claims.statement: Gluten-containing grains must be strictly avoided in celiac disease; US 'gluten-free' labeling requires <20 ppm gluten.

sources.title: Gluten-Free Labeling of Foods final rule (21 CFR 101.91)
Celiac Disease — eating, diet, and nutrition

claims.statement: No amount of alcohol is known to be safe during pregnancy; prenatal alcohol exposure is a leading preventable cause of birth defects.

sources.title: Alcohol Use During Pregnancy
Committee Opinion: At-Risk Drinking and Alcohol Dependence
